notes.title: NEWS!
notes.notes:
I have uploaded the offline demo version of AMNYAM...! Please give it a try.

link↓
https://yulugame.itch.io/amnyam

 
Aim Climb Map2 will be released on around March 30th.
 
A sequel to Aim Climb. AMNYAM has evolved casually, while Aim Climb Map2 is hardcore.
Initially, I was aiming for a slightly easier Aim Climb that could be played online, but with the addition of new skills and gimmicks that require skillful use of those skills, it has evolved in a direction that adds more enjoyable actions besides aiming at targets.
 
You can use many skills in the demo, so please try it out for yourself. I would be happy if you could enjoy it while thinking about which skills are easier to use than the conventional skills, and which ones suit you best.
 
There is also a story, but it is not intrusive. It is scattered in conversations with NPCs, so if you like, please try to guess the story of this game. If you are not interested, please skip it and climb on.
 
It is still in a playable state, and I was planning to release it immediately after Map2, but there are still more elements that can be added, so please let me work on it a little more. Please look forward to the release.
 
Also, since online system are a first for me, I would like to conduct a limited-time playtest of online play and competitive mini-games in the Steam version demo for verification purposes.
I will let you know when that will be.
 
As a rough adjustment policy, AMNYAM is about "increasing what you can do" with new skills and unique gimmicks, while Aim Climb Map2 is about "increasing what you can't do" with vicious gimmicks and high difficulty.
 
Map1 can be managed to some extent by clicking on the targets in the upward direction, but in Map2, the position of catgirl becomes important.
 
Also, Map 2 will have more high difficulty targets.
, but the high-difficulty targets on Map 1 will also be present.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42049024/94b228e201102f8baf7e6ea404ddedeadb2e4cf6.png[/img] < hi!
 
In Map2, I will lovingly destroy the user.
Looking forward to it?
 
With gratitude to the users,
YuLu

(P.S If you find any bugs or discrepancies in the translation of the AMNYAM demo, please send me a  email!)
yulsuppor@gmail.com

notes.title: Long time no see! Important announcement. The keyword is late March.
notes.notes:
It's been a while. Now that various preparations are in place, I would like to report to you. As for Aim Climb Map2, I plan to release it around late March, close to the third anniversary, along with the divided subspecies that occurred during its production.

First, let me briefly explain that subspecies.

[h1] "AMNYAM" Store Page Launched! [/h1]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2652590/AM__NYAM/
[u]！！！I would be very happy to add it to your wish list.！！！[/u]

I named it "AMNYAM," which has a cute feel to it. To put it simply, it's a more casual Aim Climb. (Multiplayer is also possible!) It is also a part that was divided during the production of Aim Climb Map2.

[b] What is division? [/b] During the production of Aim Climb Map2, I became very attached to it and was filled with the desire to add new features and make adjustments to the Aim Climb system to create a more casual experience with various ways to play. However, I also had a strong desire to maintain a consistent concept throughout the work, and I hesitated to change the direction from a hardcore concept.

Therefore, I decided to split the production concept into two and fundamentally branch out how I want to continue Aim Climb, including future policies. 
[b] These are the casual concept "AM NYAM" and the hardcore concept "Aim Climb Map2." [/b] I will release them around late March simultaneously.

I hope casual gamers will definitely enjoy "AMNYAM" as a continuation! I researched and created it so that players can enjoy the flow of "Aim's skill test" → "New gimmick operation check" → "Practice," gradually increasing the difficulty with each stage. NPCs also exist, enhancing the adventure elements.


Hardcore gamers, please look forward to "Aim Climb Map2." Oh, be prepared.
Since it is a stage unlocked after clearing Map1, the structure is designed with the assumption that you have the basics to climb.
(I would be happy if you could also check out AM NYAM! The highest difficulty is quite challenging.)

The music is created with particular attention to match the atmosphere of the stages. Since the cave concept has been abandoned, there are more up-tempo songs. I also tried using live drum sounds. Stay tuned.

AMNYAM and Aim Climb Map 2 will be released on a different date. The reason for the delay is that I am the only support person for Aim Climb Map2, so bug fixes and other support will be out of order. (I was up all night when Aim Climb was released...) Aim Climb Map2 will be released around late March.AM NYAM may be warmed up a little. I will let you know as soon as it is decided.

Now, here is some supplementary information. I will explain the differences in the AMNYAM system.

AMNYAM is designed to cater to casual gamers, focusing on having many users play outside the game and minimizing elements that lead to a rapid increase in difficulty within the game. Below are some examples.

[b] Multilingual Support [/b]
Aim Climb is composed of handwritten characters and some digital characters, making multilingual support extremely difficult as elements increase. (Especially handwritten characters)
Therefore, AM NYAM has completely transitioned to digital characters and has fully adopted a system that incorporates prepared external data files. (This is what I wanted to do the most by separating the games.)
This allows for multilingual support, enabling more users to recognize the text, and as an extension of that, NPCs exist. Various characters will speak!

[b] Elimination of Screen Transitions During Stage Changes [/b]
Aim Climb is designed to load stages in small segments, and the skills required for those transitions significantly raise the difficulty curve. I enjoy the thrill of lightly grasping the layout of the next area or requiring quick flick aiming, but it is not very casual. Therefore, in AM NYAM, I have abolished this, and the same stage will be loaded all at once, with the transition to the next stage warping to the platform of that stage. (Aim Climb Map2 will naturally follow the Aim Climb system, so be prepared.)

[b] Multiplayer! [/b]
This was part of the initial concept for Aim Climb, but I gave up due to a lack of technical skills. In AM NYAM, I am focusing on code work with multiplayer in mind, such as making the target's movement coordinate-controlled. (Aim Climb uses speed control. Due to the influence of delay correction, there is a possibility of position shifting, so I would like to transition to coordinate control in future updates for Aim Climb as well. However, since it may affect RTA players who compete for time by repeatedly playing the game (thank you for playing a lot), I want to carefully transition and revert as much as possible while discussing with them to ensure the position does not change too much.)
I also plan to implement or add a mini-game-like competitive mode in updates.
Since multiplayer is an unfamiliar technology, I would like to keep AM NYAM in early access and gradually refine it while exchanging opinions with users.

There are many small differences, such as the existence of items.

There are countless small details, so I will conclude here. This has turned into quite a lengthy message. Thank you for reading this far.
This is the first update in about nine months.

With gratitude to the users,
YuLu
(PS. I changed my name a bit. Yul → YuLu. The reason is that I can't tell the difference between the lowercase "l" and the uppercase "I." It's not a big deal. )

notes.title: High difficulty targets, fixed patterns
notes.notes:
It is still very cold in some areas. Please take care of your health.

This is a small update for AimClimb.

AimClimb was designed with mouse control in mind, but I've made a few changes to the movement of objects to make it more route-oriented and more enjoyable to repeat.

The changes are as follows

[h3]1, Fixed the pattern of the flick-like (question icon) teleportation target.[/h3]
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/42049024/94b228e201102f8baf7e6ea404ddedeadb2e4cf6.png[/img]

The target moves when clicked and is a high difficulty target that requires flick-aim, but with this update I have fixed the pattern of where the target moves to so that players who are not good at flicking the mouse or players who value repeatability can play along.
If you keep in mind that the first flick will always go to the bottom left, this will make it a little easier to aim on the fly.
(It's a loop: bottom left, top right, top left, bottom right, left, right, down, up).

[h3]2, Fixed the movement pattern of the lelele-like (broom icon).[/h3]
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/42049024/0c12db17a1064c9b300cc50651a76ac943d5f89e.png[/img]

The lelele-like moves right to left and left to right, but I made a pattern of simple movements.
The movement was a little awkward when the movements were all the same, so only the cycle was shifted by -0.1 to +0.1 seconds depending on the location.
　　
[h3]3, The target generation pattern of the generative target (the grey square target) was fixed.[/h3]
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/42049024/92589316925db24ee8bc21cc62fbafe3dfba640b.png[/img]

[h3]4，In the waterfall stage (stage 5), fixed so that the lelele target is always affected by the waterfall.[/h3]

Occasionally, the lelele target would leave the flowing waterfall, escape the effect of the waterfall and stop moving downwards, often lagging behind the cycle of the flowing target. Therefore, the risk of this misalignment was eliminated by constantly reflecting the effect of the waterfall.

These are four points.
I will design the upcoming new map with an emphasis on mouse operation, but also with an emphasis on reproducibility.

With thanks to game users
Yul

notes.title: MAP2 Production has begun!
notes.notes:
It is suddenly getting chilly, so please take care of yourself.
Now, here is an announcement from Aim Climb.

[u]MAP2 Production has begun! [/u]

New stages, new gimmicks, new targets, new BGM, etc.
I will produce it with great care.

Look forward to it!

I am going to work on it in parallel with the development of other games[u](look forward to this one too!)[/u]
, so it will take some time.

(I am testing the map selection screen from the current version).

[u]Also, as a game clearing remedy, I would consider implementing checkpoints![/u]

This is a remedy for players who want to complete the story on their own, so when using checkpoints, the STEAM achievement will not be unlocked upon completion.

Also, I plan to set a limit on the number of times a player can complete a checkpoint, since the thrill of falling should not be lost.
I will make adjustments after repeated trial runs.


Thank you to all the users.
Yul

notes.notes:
"Sensitivity adjustment function" has been implemented!
Sensitivity can be adjusted from the settings screen.


Other updates

The clear time is now displayed when clearing any difficulty level. (Measurement will start from the current patch, so accurate times will be available from the next climb.)

Following the above, the current climbing time is now displayed when loading.(measurements started from the current patch)

The number of times each difficulty level has been cleared is now displayed. (measurements started from the current patch)

Steam screenshots are now available. (default on steam is F12).

The above. Four updates.
The sensitivity adjustment function has been requested by many users since the first release, but it took a long time to implement due to personal development. But now it is finally implemented! （It's been a long time.)

Thank you for playing Aim Climb.

Yul

notes.title: Summary of recent updates
notes.notes:
{1}After clearing any difficulty level of Aim Climb, the "Back Story" can now be viewed to learn more about the world of Aim Climb. Available by clicking on the book under Trophies.

{2}Following on from the above, one of the endings prepared for Aim Climb has been greatly increased in volume and made into a "true ending" that sums up the world view of Aim Climb.

{3}Redefined the differences in behavior depending on the operating environment.

{4}Fixed the problem where the actual volume was not changed when restarting after adjusting the volume, even though the volume was notated as changed.

These were the four notices. A soundtrack is being produced upon request. 
Thank you for playing Aim Climb.
Thank you for your continued support of Aim Climb.

Yul
